newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore eases restrictions on Far East Review.
newsitem.headline: Singapore eases restrictions on Far East Review.

text.p: Singapore said on Thursday it is further easing restrictions on the Far Eastern Economic Review (FEER) by allowing its circulation in the city state to increase to 8,000 copies from 6,000.

The Ministry of Information and the Arts (MITA) said the change, effective from July 1, followed a review of the circulation of the Hong Kong-based FEER, which remains a gazetted (restricted) publication.
Singapore gazetted FEER, a weekly news magazine owned by Dow Jones and Co Inc in December 1987 and slashed its circulation of 10,000 per issue after accusing it of interference in domestic politics.
FEER then announced it would not circulate at all in Singapore until the restriction was completely lifted.
In June 1991, MITA agreed to an application by the magazine that it be allowed to circulate 110 copies at Changi airport.
MITA subsequently allowed further increases in the magazine's circulation.
